r1_cite: fastapi/routing.py:188-215; probe: body b'{"client_name":"\xff",...}' gives 400 {"detail":"There was an error parsing the body"}; invalid JSON with Early-Data: 1 gives 422, not 425
r1_finding: Two body-reading branches are wrong or missing: a JSON body that json.loads cannot decode as text (invalid UTF-8) raises UnicodeDecodeError, which FastAPI turns into 400 {"detail":"There was an error parsing the body"} (Go's decoder would accept it); and the body is read before any dependency, so invalid JSON (422) and the 400 win over the 0-RTT 425, while pydantic field errors come after it. Correct: read and decode the body first (422 jsondecode / 400 parse error), then the 0-RTT check, then model validation.
r2_cite: fastapi/routing.py:188-218; probe: body b'{"client_name":"\xff"}' gives 400; body '{bad' with Early-Data: 1 gives 422, '{}' with Early-Data: 1 gives 425
r2_finding: Two body cases are missing. (1) A body that json.loads cannot decode as text (for example invalid UTF-8) raises an error that is not JSONDecodeError, so FastAPI returns 400 {"detail":"There was an error parsing the body"}. Go's encoding/json accepts invalid UTF-8, so the handler must check for it. (2) FastAPI parses the body before the app-wide 0-RTT dependency runs, so a JSON decode error gives 422 even with Early-Data: 1. Only a body that parses, valid or not, gets the 425. Body parsing must happen before the 0-RTT check, or the 0-RTT middleware must let the 422 and 400 cases go first.

r1_finding: The 401 detail is not always "Invalid HTTP sig": enforce_httpsig writes "Unsupported signature algorithm, must be rsa-sha256 or hs2019" when is_unsupported_algorithm and "Signature expired" when is_expired (httpsig.py:300-306). Correct: 403 {"detail":"Blocked"}, 202 {"detail":"Accepted"} for a gone actor, else 401 with one of those three details, as the shared enforce_httpsig middleware writes it.
